task.description: Gate REQ-231 (Entities.Query.Cursor generalized keyset-pagination codec + Entities.Query.FieldGrants default-deny field-level redaction, two new tenant-scoped tables) against security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8, with independent verification of tenant isolation, the default-deny redaction logic's three cases, the redaction sentinel's leak-freedom, the cursor's dynamic-query injection surface, the Ecto.UUID.dump!/1 addition's failure behavior, absence of raw SQL, and absence of any route/controller.

result.note:
INV-1 (tenant data isolation) APPLIES -- both new migrations (priv/repo/migrations/20260907010001_create_entity_field_restrictions.exs, .../20260907010002_create_user_entity_grants.exs) are gated by the mandatory `if prefix() do` guard, create their tables inside `prefix: schema`, and are registered in Letflow.TenantProvisioning's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (verified in git diff) and test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's @expected_tenant_tables (both halves of (b) confirmed). All FieldGrants/Cursor queries pass `prefix: prefix` to Repo.all/Repo.all (field_grants.ex:98, cursor.ex:137) -- confirmed (a). No caller-supplied tenant_id column exists on either table (entity_field_restrictions has none; user_entity_grants' user_id FK is scoped by the resolved prefix's own users table, not a separate cross-schema value) -- (c) satisfied trivially, no tenant_id column present to misattribute. PASS.

INV-2, INV-3, INV-5: NOT-APPLICABLE (S4/S5 not started; confirmed no route/controller file added -- `grep -rln 'Query.Cursor\|Query.FieldGrants' lib/letflow/routers/ web/` returned nothing, `git diff --stat` for lib/letflow/routers/ and web/ is empty).

INV-4 (secrets by reference): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no secret material resolved, logged, or threaded through any new code.

INV-6: satisfied by this handoff itself.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) APPLIES: `grep -rn Repo.query` across both migrations and both new modules returned zero hits. Both new tables use `Ecto.Migration`'s `create table/2` DSL (no raw SQL). Cursor.ex's JSONB cast fragments (@string_fragment/@integer_fragment/etc, lines 403-408) are compile-time module-attribute literals with `?` placeholders bound via `fragment(literal, r.field_values, ^field_name)` -- field_name itself is not raw caller text but the `name` of an already-Allowlist-resolved field (REQ-230's allowlist, already reviewed). No string concatenation or interpolation anywhere in the new code. PASS.

INV-1's redaction-specific central property -- default-deny correctness in FieldGrants.load_restrictions/3 -- traced line-by-line (field_grants.ex:84-101): the query is `entity_field_restrictions AS fr LEFT JOIN user_entity_grants AS g ON (g.entity_type,g.field_name)=(fr.entity_type,fr.field_name) AND g.user_id=^user_id WHERE fr.entity_type=^entity_type AND is_nil(g.id)`, selecting fr.field_name into the restriction_set. Three cases traced: (1) field with NO entity_field_restrictions row -> never appears in `fr` at all -> never selected -> absent from restriction_set -> redact_field_values/2 (field_grants.ex:113-121) leaves it untouched -> VISIBLE. This is default-allow only for fields nobody ever declared restricted, matching the design's own explicit §3.2 semantics (verified against lib/letflow/design/req231-entity-query-cursor-field-grants.md lines 333-373: 'A field with no entity_field_restrictions row is visible to every user unconditionally'), not an inverted-boolean bug against the design's contract. (2) field WITH a restriction row and NO matching user_entity_grants row for this user -> LEFT JOIN finds no g row -> g.id IS NULL -> WHERE clause keeps it -> field_name selected into restriction_set -> redact_field_values/2 replaces its value with :__field_redacted__, key retained -> REDACTED (default-deny confirmed). (3) field WITH a restriction row AND a matching grant row for this user -> LEFT JOIN finds g -> g.id IS NOT NULL -> WHERE clause's is_nil(g.id) excludes this row -> field_name NOT selected -> absent from restriction_set -> VISIBLE (override confirmed). All three cases produce the design's intended fail-safe behavior; no fail-open path found.

Redaction sentinel leak-freedom: redact_field_values/2 (field_grants.ex:112-121) is a pure Map.new/2 over field_values with no I/O, no conditional early-return, no lazy/streaming evaluation -- every key is either passed through unchanged or has its value fully replaced by the atom :__field_redacted__ before the function returns; there is no code path that reads the original value into a log, error message, or a different key. redact_page/2 (field_grants.ex:130-138) only calls redact_field_values/2 per item; no other field of the Latest struct (id, inserted_at, etc.) is touched, matching the design's structural-metadata carve-out (design doc lines 433-436). No leak surface found.

Cursor codec dynamic-query injection surface: apply_resume_filter/build_row_dynamic (cursor.ex:311-337) composes nested dynamic/2 exclusively from (a) `term.dyn`, itself built earlier from either `dynamic([r], field(r, ^column_atom))` for typed columns (an atom resolved from Allowlist.typed_columns/0, REQ-230's closed table -- never caller text) or a fragment call using one of six fixed compile-time literal SQL strings (cursor.ex:403-408) with the field name interpolated only via `?`/`^field_name` parameter binding, and (b) `^value`/`^maybe_dump(...)`, always an Elixir term bound as a query parameter, never string-concatenated into any fragment literal. `resolve_sort/2` (cursor.ex:196-207) rejects any sort field not already in the Allowlist (REQ-230, previously reviewed) before any dynamic is built. No string concatenation, no runtime-built fragment literal, no path from decoded cursor JSON values to a SQL string -- all decoded values enter only as bound parameters via `^`. No injection surface found, independent of REQ-230's own prior PASS.

Ecto.UUID.dump!/1 addition (maybe_dump/2, cursor.ex:353-356): confirmed by direct execution (`MIX_ENV=test mix run --no-start` against `Ecto.UUID.dump!("not-a-uuid")`) that malformed input raises a clean `ArgumentError: cannot dump given UUID to binary` -- no type confusion, no exploitable memory/behavior beyond a raised exception. This IS reachable from network input: a cursor is only prefix+expiry-checked (Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4), not cryptographically signed, so a caller can supply a JSON resume-key array whose final ('id') element is a non-UUID string, and `decode_component(:string, id_value)` (cursor.ex:306) accepts any binary without UUID-format validation, so this raise is realistically triggerable, not merely a theoretical/malformed-JSON case already rejected earlier. However: (1) this exact class of behavior -- an unsigned, prefix-checked-only cursor whose decoded components are used in `Repo` calls without further format validation, with malformed input raising an unhandled exception (e.g. `Letflow.Entities.Definitions`'s own already-merged, already-reviewed `list_definitions/2` cursor path raises `ArgumentError` via `String.to_integer/1` on a malformed timestamp component at definitions.ex:344, and its `{^inserted_at, ^id}` comparison would raise on a malformed UUID id via Ecto's own automatic dump on query execution) -- is pre-existing, already-shipped, already-SECURITY-REVIEWER-passed precedent in this codebase, not a new risk class introduced by this diff; (2) each HTTP request in this stack runs in its own isolated process, so an unhandled exception here degrades only that one caller's request (translated to a 500 by the standard Plug/Phoenix error boundary) and cannot cross tenant boundaries or take down another tenant's in-flight work -- this is exactly the case INV-8's own text carves out as acceptable ('let a doomed process crash' vs 'crash a shared process that takes down unrelated tenants' work'); (3) no tenant data is exposed by the crash (a 500 with a generic message, not a leaked value). This does not rise to a BLOCKER-level INV-8 violation given the established precedent and per-request isolation, but is noted here as a robustness observation: ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER may wish to have `decode_component(:string, ...)` for an :binary_id-typed sort/id component validate UUID format (or wrap `maybe_dump/2`'s dump call) to return `{:error, :invalid_cursor}` instead of raising, for defense-in-depth consistency with the tagged-tuple style the rest of `build_resume_terms/2` already uses -- recommended as a follow-up, not a merge blocker.

INV-8 general: `grep -rn '^\s*{:ok, .*} = '` over the two new modules found no bare-pattern-match-on-external-I/O violations; all Repo/decode paths use `with`/case tagged-tuple handling except the one dump! call discussed above.

Own verification run (fresh, this review): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> clean, no output. `mix test test/letflow/entities/query_cursor_field_grants_test.exs --max-cases 1` -> 'Result: 8 passed', 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/entities/ --max-cases 1` -> 'Result: 137 passed'. `mix test test/letflow/api/ --max-cases 1` -> 'Result: 176 passed' (no stale tenant_template schema issue hit this run). All match ELIXIR-DEV's reported figures.

Verdict: PASS. No BLOCKER-severity invariant violation found. One non-blocking robustness observation (Ecto.UUID.dump!/1's raise on malformed cursor id component) flagged above for optional follow-up.
